issues.description: Class de.tum.in.ase.eist.service.PersonService: the template defines a constructor accepting a PersonRepository (public PersonService(PersonRepository personRepository)) to enable constructor-based dependency injection, whereas the solution defines a no-argument constructor (public PersonService()) that sets the repository field to null. This divergence breaks the expected dependency injection pattern and will cause NullPointerExceptions when methods in PersonService use personRepository (for example save/delete/getById). It also conflicts with the exercise's layered design where PersonService is provided the repository by Spring.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signatures consistent. Restore constructor-based injection in the solution by replacing the no-arg constructor with public PersonService(PersonRepository personRepository) { this.personRepository = personRepository; } so Spring can inject the repository and the service methods operate on a non-null personRepository. Alternatively, if a different DI approach is intended, update the template and problem statement to document that approach and ensure the repository is properly injected.
